output:
**★☆☆☆☆ Good software, no support when it counts**

*Bridger Bend Community Library, Montana · One branch, 2 full-time staff plus volunteers, about 2,300 active cardholders*

I'm writing this review a few weeks later than I meant to because I wanted to be calm when I did it. Here is where things stand.

We signed a three-year contract with Stackhouse Cloud in June 2026 at $14,200 a year. Migration went live October 19. On October 28, circulation stopped working properly. Since then, the only way we can check items out is offline on a single laptop. Our holds queue was wiped, about 640 holds gone.

We have had a support ticket open for 12 days. In that time we've received three replies, and every one said the issue had been "escalated to engineering." Nothing after that.

During the sales process we were promised a dedicated migration specialist. What we got was a shared inbox.

Here is what that means on the ground. A retired rancher drove 40 minutes to pick up the large-print Westerns he had on hold. We had no record of the hold and had to send him home empty-handed. Our volunteer has been writing checkouts on index cards. For a library our size, these patrons aren't statistics. We know them by name.

To be fair, the product itself isn't the problem. The demo was impressive, and the staff interface is better than our old system's. I still think Stackhouse could be a good fit for small libraries. The failure is in support, and for a library with two full-time staff, support is the part we depend on most.

Timing matters too. Our county budget hearing is November 18 and our line item is on the agenda. I would like to be able to tell our commissioners this is resolved.

**To Stackhouse:** I'm asking for a named person with real authority to call me this week. Not another ticket update. A phone call.

**To other directors, especially at small libraries:** before you sign, get support response times in writing. Ask what happens if your system goes down after go-live, who specifically you'll be talking to, and how quickly. Don't accept "dedicated specialist" unless the contract says what that means.

One star for now. If Stackhouse fixes this and makes it right, I will gladly come back and update this review.

*Director, Bridger Bend Community Library*

---

That's about 390 words. A couple of notes. I left the sign-off as your title only, so add your name if you want it there. If anything changes before you post, like a reply on the ticket or a lost hold turning up, update the numbers so the review stays accurate.
